name: Bambu Lab X1 series toolhead
source: Nozzle outline and housing boxes adapted from PancakeSlicer head envelope bambu-x1-p1 (AGPL-3.0, github.com/ZimengXiong/PancakeSlicer, engine/resources/nonplanar/heads, clone 174a578f43), whose nozzle bands come from a community hotend CAD (printables.com/model/533213) and whose housing, duct, sock and carriage boxes are that author's estimates. The nozzle profile here is the outer radius of each of their bands taken at the band's lower edge (conservative). Gantry rod height 34 mm is Bambu's extruder_clearance_height_to_rod from the BBL machine profile; its Y span is estimated. Heater block and sock bottom: 2.5 mm above the tip, measured by the owner on an X1 Carbon (nozzle tip to sock, 2026-11-15); was 4 mm in the PancakeSlicer estimate. The sock's X/Y extent and every other part are still estimates; the X1 and X1E are assumed to share the toolhead (not checked).

curved_tops.verified_note: Owner's print (2026-11-17, Bambu PLA) of the arm with the ladder file 07e settings (3 curved layers, max angle 10, material beside allowed): nozzle tip up to 0.44 mm and flank up to 0.43 mm in the flat top-surface material along the patch edge, sock 0.88 mm clear, clean print (its curved part, 1.78 mm at 10.0 deg, is within the rise and slope below). Earlier (2026-11-16): owner's print of CurvedTops_Dome40_X1C (40 mm puck, 1.8 mm spherical cap, edge slope 10.3 deg, 3 curved layers, 0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C, Bambu PLA Basic) came out good. Curved tops was planned with 2.0 mm allowed rise (sock 2.5 mm less 0.5 mm margin).
